Heads up — over this morning's batch window we're seeing a noticeable latency spike for a subset of generation requests routed to the redwood-4o endpoint. Typical p95 is <2s; between ~08:55–09:20 PDT ~5–30% of requests spiked to 20–30s. This is impacting downstream processing and causing retries.

Quick details:
- Environment: production (us-west-2)
- Model: redwood-4o (default route)
- Approx affected fraction: ~25% of requests in the window
- Example request IDs: 7f2b9a1e, c3d4f8b2, 1a9e7c44
- Example prompt lengths: 120–600 tokens (most around 180)

We've attached a short text log with request ids and client-side durations. No JVM OOMs or container restarts on our side. Can you confirm whether there were infra events or rate-limiting on your end? Happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Simon

Subject: Outcome: analysis of 2026-07-27 batch latency window

Hi Simon — thank you for the prompt logs and for offering the synthetic run. Engineering completed an initial investigation and summary below. TL;DR: we did not find an internal platform error or capacity saturation in Redwood; the observed delays are consistent with client-side request coalescing and retry behaviour interacting with TCP connection queuing.

What we did:
- Correlated your provided request IDs with our ingress and model-side traces (attached).
- Evaluated per-shard GPU busy/queue lengths and scheduler metrics for us-west-2 across the window. No host OOMs, no throttles, and GPU p95 kernel time remained stable.
- Checked recent deployments: none in the 24h prior.

What we observed:
- Ingress timing: for the affected request IDs the request reached our edge quickly but experienced 12–18s of queueing before worker assignment. Redwood's worker-side inference times remained normal (p95 inference ~1.8s).
- Client behaviour: your log shows a short-duration connection coalescer that batches bursts into a small pool of HTTP/1.1 connections. Under steady bursts this can cause head-of-line queueing at the TCP connection and local request buffer, which matches the 20–30s end-to-end times you saw when combined with client retries.

Resolution / next steps:
1) We recommend temporarily disabling the local coalescer or increasing connection concurrency for the batch window to avoid head-of-line queuing; this should prevent the long tail immediately.
2) We can run a joint synthetic test at your proposed time to validate.
3) Internally, Marcus and Karthik will monitor the scheduler heuristics and add an alert if ingress queue time exceeds 5s for sustained periods.

We've attached the filtered Redwood trace for the example IDs: redwood_trace_20260727.txt. That file contains per-hop timestamps and worker assignment markers. There were no error responses or tokenization anomalies logged on our side.

If you'd like we can schedule a 30-min troubleshooting session to walk through the client-side config and to run the synthetic load together. Otherwise we'll track this as an open support follow-up and close the incident when we validate the mitigation.

Thanks again — please let me know which you'd prefer.

—Grace
